round_3_disposition.summary: check-secrets.sh fails open in diff mode over untracked files: scan_files is called and nothing checks `scanned`
round_3_disposition.disposition: FIXED, and the finding UNDERSTATED it. Reproduced both arms: diff mode exits 0 with a ghp_ token in an untracked file, and full-tree mode does too, because the round-2 call-site guard runs several lines BEFORE the untracked scan and counts only the tracked pass. Fixing the diff arm alone would have been the third patch to an instance, so the guard moved INSIDE scan_files and the redundant call-site guard was removed. Accounts for deliberate skips (the detector's own files, binaries) so an all-binary untracked set still passes -- proved by a case. Mutation control: with the new guard disabled, three suite cases go red.

round_3_disposition.summary: the Assert-Ok coverage analysis misses six of seven command forms, including `& $tool`, `.\tool.exe` and column 0
round_3_disposition.disposition: FIXED. Reproduced the reviewer's table exactly (1 caught, 6 missed) -- after discarding my own first attempt, which inserted the command where it displaced cargo fmt's Assert-Ok and so read all-CAUGHT for the wrong reason. Rule inverted: a line is a command UNLESS it is a recognised construct. Keyword boundary is ([^[:alnum:]_-]|$), not \b, because in awk \b is a backspace (gawk spells it \y; this runner is mawk 1.3.4) -- writing \b silently produced three false positives. Controls added for all seven forms and for twelve constructs; with the old analysis restored, six form cases go red.
